title: JudgeBench: which of two responses is correct?
decision: which of two responses to a question is the correct one (objective correctness label of the data set)

source.name: JudgeBench (JudgeBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-based Judges, arXiv:2410.12784)

notes: All usable pairs of both splits (620 in the files; no sampling). Dropped: 0 (label is not a strict preference); 0 (a response longer than 12,000 characters); 1 (the two responses are identical). Gold A 310, B 309 (gpt: 175 / 175; claude: 135 / 134): the order of the two responses was drawn anew per row with random.Random(20261007) so that the correct one is first in half of the rows of each split; meta.order names the source fields shown as response A and B, meta.source_label is the label of the file. Rows by origin of the question (meta.source; the 14 mmlu-pro subjects together): livebench-math 90, livebench-reasoning 149, livecodebench 72, mmlu-pro 308. Both responses of a pair are written by the same model (meta.response_model: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 in split gpt, claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 in split claude); correctness comes from the scoring of the source sets, not from human judges of the responses; several pairs can share one question. The licence recorded here is that of the JudgeBench card; the licences of the sets the questions come from (meta.source) were not checked.
